sources.citation: Smith, Kenneth D. 1973. More on Sedang ethnodialects. Mon-Khmer Studies 4: 43-51.
sources.note: Only about Sedang: 'The unstressed presyllable ko- occurs in the terms for dialects 1, 2, 4 to 6' (p.44). Monom is not named; the Mang Buk 'koleq' dialect (no register contrast, retains final stops) is left unidentified.

sources.note: Lists Mơ Nâm only as a local group name under Xơ Đăng; no linguistic data.

sources.citation: Cheeseman, Nathaniel, Jennifer Herington & Paul Sidwell. 2013. Bahnaric linguistic bibliography with selected annotations. Mon-Khmer Studies 42: xxxiv-lxvii (in the open MKS 42 volume).
sources.note: No phonology content for Monom; bibliographic pointers only (no Monom-specific grammar, phonology or wordlist publication is indexed). General remark that Bahnaric languages are not tonal but many contrast two phonation types is made of the branch, not of Monom.
sources.venue: Mon-Khmer Studies 42: xxxiv-lxvii (in the open MKS 42 volume)

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A., Kenneth J. Gregerson & Paul Sidwell. 2011. The North Bahnaric clade: a computational approach. In Sophana Srichampa, Paul Sidwell & Kenneth Gregerson (eds.), Austroasiatic Studies: papers from ICAAL4 (Mon-Khmer Studies Journal Special Issue No. 3 = Pacific Linguistics E-9), 33-47. Dallas: SIL / Canberra: PL / Salaya: Mahidol.
sources.note: Nothing. Monom/Monam and Bonam are taxa in a Bayesian lexical phylogeny (Monam-Bonam sister pair); data drawn from unpublished 'Monam 2007. Ms.' and 'Monam list SIL unknown. Ms.'; p.34 'Monom, Katua, and Takua are of more uncertain status'. No word-structure or stress statement for Monom.

sources.citation: Srichampa, Sophana & Paul Sidwell (eds.). 2011. Austroasiatic Studies: papers from ICAAL4. MKS Special Issue No. 2 (= PL E-8).
sources.note: No Monom content (downloaded with vol. 2; text-searched).

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2009. How many branches in a tree? Cua and East (North) Bahnaric. In Bethwyn Evans (ed.), Discovering history through language: papers in honour of Malcolm Ross, 193-204. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 605.
sources.note: Name in a classification list only; the paper's phonological argument concerns Cua and Kơtua (nasal hardening, lack of register); nothing on Monom stress or tone.
sources.venue: Discovering history through language: papers in honour of Malcolm Ross

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2002. Genetic classification of the Bahnaric languages: a comprehensive review. Mon-Khmer Studies 32: 1-24.
sources.note: Nothing; Monom appears only in the North Bahnaric membership list (Fig. 4).

sources.citation: Smith, Kenneth D. 1979. Sedang grammar: phonological and syntactic structure. Pacific Linguistics B-50. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Phonology is of Central Sedang only; 'Monam' is merely listed among North Bahnaric languages in ch. 3. No Monom data.

sources.citation: Gregerson, Kenneth J. & Kenneth D. Smith. 1973. The development of Tơdrah register. Mon-Khmer Studies 4: 143-184.
sources.note: Describes Todrah (unstressed presyllable + stressed main syllable); 'MONAM' appears only as a label on the location map (per SEAlang SALA full-text index). Nothing on Monom stress.

sources.citation: Smith, Kenneth D. 1972. A phonological reconstruction of Proto-North-Bahnaric. (Language Data, Asian-Pacific Series 2.) Santa Ana: SIL.
sources.note: p.1 'All words in these languages have a stressed main syllable (tonique); many words also have an unstressed presyllable' -- said of the North Bahnaric languages he lists (Bahnar, Rengao, Sedang, Todrah, Halang, Jeh, Hrê, Kotua, Cua); Monom is not among them and is not mentioned.
sources.venue: (Language Data, Asian-Pacific Series 2.) Santa Ana: SIL

sources.citation: Thomas, David D. 1966. Mon-Khmer subgroupings in Vietnam. In N. Zide (ed.), Studies in Comparative Austroasiatic Linguistics, 194-202. The Hague: Mouton; and Thomas, David. 1973. A note on the branches of Mon-Khmer. MKS 4: 139-141.
sources.note: SEAlang SALA full-text hits for exact word 'Monom' show it only in lexicostatistic cognate-percentage tables / branch lists; not phonological.

sources.citation: Wilson, Ruth S. 1966. A comparison of Muong with some Mon-Khmer languages. In Norman H. Zide (ed.), Studies in Comparative Austroasiatic Linguistics (Indo-Iranian Monographs 5), 203-213. The Hague: Mouton.
sources.note: Nothing on Bonam/Monom prosody or word structure. A Muong-centred cognate list in which about fifteen Bonam citation forms appear (several sesquisyllabic in shape, e.g. katop, kachet, kachii, di?dong), drawn from unpublished SIL survey lists; the only general remark on syllable structure (contraction of first syllables of disyllables, p.212) is about Muong vs Mon-Khmer generally. Value: the only open publication seen that prints any Monom (Bonam) word forms; no stress or tone statement.
sources.venue: Studies in Comparative Austroasiatic Linguistics (Indo-Iranian Monographs 5)

sources.citation: Any Vietnamese provincial/Institute of Linguistics report on 'tiếng Mơ Nâm' (Kon Tum, Xơ Đăng local group Mơ Nâm), e.g. by Tạ Văn Thông / Tạ Quang Tùng (Viện Ngôn ngữ học / Viện Từ điển học và Bách khoa thư).

sources.note: Vietnamese state projects on Xơ Đăng local-group languages (Tơ Đrá, Mơ Nâm, Ca Dong, Ha Lăng) sometimes include a phonology chapter; coccoc/vjol/luanan.nlv searches found nothing).

sources.citation: 'Monam 2007. Ms.' -- Kon Tum fieldwork wordlist (Edmondson/Gregerson with Vietnamese Institute of Linguistics colleagues), cited as a data source in Edmondson, Gregerson & Sidwell 2011:47 ('full details or images supplied on request').

sources.note: Most recent first-hand Monom data; field notes may include remarks on word shape (sesquisyllabic, main-syllable stress). Obtainable only from the authors/Sidwell.
